pages.text: What about your dream? Are you going to quit?

pages.text: IF YOU KEEP WOODY AND THE OTHERS SO MAD AT YOU, AREN'T WE GOING TO HAVE A LOT OF LONELINESS?

pages.text: PUTTING ON A FAKE SMILE AND ACTING LIKE YOU'RE FIN...

pages.text: COOL-SEEK, I TOLD HIM NOT TO TALK ABOUT HIS THINGS TODAY.

pages.text: Do you think we should tell the police?

pages.text: No, I don't want to get caught.

pages.text: Let's just keep it between us.

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: IT LOOKS LIKE THEY'RE GOING TO FOLLOW HER IN LIEU OF A REAL PERSON IN THIS PLACE.

pages.text: I GET THE FEELING THAT YOU ARE BEING SCARED OF HER...

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: YOU GOT SOME REASON FOR THAT?

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: I HAVE TO MENTOR SANSO-CHAN. AND OF COURSE I PLAN TO TAKE MY POSITION.

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: WITH THE SUPPORT OF MY MOTHER, I STARTED A SNACK BAR.

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: MY MOTHER HAD LEFT HER BROTHER AND HER SISTER-BROTHER.

pages.text: JOINING THE CHOP-IN-FANATIC CCG ACADEMY JUNIOR SCHOOL.

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: WHILE SHE STILL HAD NO INTENTION OF BECOMING AN OFFICIAL WATASHIGIRI.

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: JUST LIKE HOW THEIR CAREER PATHS APPROACHED.

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: THAT WAS THE TIME WHEN I MET THEM.

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: AND THEY BOTH APPEALED TO ME.

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: SO I DECIDED TO JOIN THEM.

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: BUT I DIDN'T KNOW THAT I WAS ABOUT TO BECOME A SECTION VESTIGATOR.

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: EVEN IF I KNEW THAT MY CLASS-MATE WAS THE PRINCE, WELL, IT WAS STILL RIGHT!

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: SHIPPING THEIR GAMES TO LEICESTER TOO.

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: IT SEEMS THAT THE EXPLANATION OF THE PRINCE WAS NEVER READIED HER MOTHER'S EARS...

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: I can't help but think how much I've changed since I was her age.

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: She's the only one of her parents' friends who isn't even one of her parents' friends anymore.

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: Just recall that she doesn't have any family left. That doesn't mean you're happy, does it?

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: If she had any memories retained...

pages.speaker: Sassan
pages.text: It's ridiculous, but if you don't know anything about your own parents, then you don't know anything at all.
